notes: All 28 beads sit at layers 6 and 7 because their deps are the M0 Gauntlet base (BD-025 at layer 4, N38-REF and the registry skeletons at 5); 67 of 68 edges are real, and the transitive duplicates (BD-025 and STD-E2E beside N38a-09 on the pilots, BD-025 and STD-TEST beside N12-41) are real and cost nothing. The layer-6 cutoff cannot be broken here without changing BD-025 or N38-REF themselves: the one edge that frees a layer is N38b-18 to N34-11. The bigger costs on this list are calendar time, not layers: N38a-09 (197 direct dependents) and N12-41 (nine sections) are full-size beads whose dependents need only their schema and loader, so a skeleton split helps on day one even though the layer number stays the same. The more common defect is the opposite of an excess edge: checks that read files other beads fill (gate rows, public refusal rows, the reason enum), with no edge to those beads. In each case the fix that keeps the graph shallow is convention 7, moving the check to a later bead that already has both. N36-01 to BD-002 is probably unused (nothing of BD-002's nine registries or documents is read) but removing it gains no layer, so it is kept. N36-02's acceptance item 'the loader is used ... by the target register' checks a later bead (N36-01) and breaks convention 7. N19c-33 registers 'an identifier of set C', which collides with the PILOT-C-<nn> construction form of N38a-09's grammar.
